skill.name: gmail-automation
skill.description: Automates Gmail workflows through Rube MCP, including search, labels, drafts, sending, replies, and attachments.
skill.summary: Use Rube MCP to search, draft, send, reply, label, and inspect Gmail messages.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby shell, reconnaissance, and hardcoded URL detections are false positives caused by Markdown documentation and Gmail workflow examples. The skill still carries meaningful Gmail-account risk because it enables outbound email, destructive label changes, bulk mailbox updates, attachment access, and third-party OAuth through Rube MCP. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: High-impact Gmail actions lack consistent approval requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before sending emails or replies, deleting labels, bulk modifying messages, archiving, marking read or unread, or downloading attachments.

remediation.issue: Third-party OAuth dependency needs stronger consent guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Document Gmail OAuth scopes, data flow through Rube and Composio, revocation steps, and least-privilege account guidance.

remediation.issue: Bulk mailbox changes can affect many messages at once.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run summaries with message counts and representative subjects before any batch label, archive, or read-state update.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Gmail connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `gmail`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `GMAIL_SEARCH_PEOPLE` - Resolve contact name to email address [Optional]
- `is_html`: Must be `true` if body contains HTML markup
- `attachment`: Object with `{s3key, mimetype, name}` from prior download
- At least one of `recipient_email`, `cc`, or `bcc` required
- At least one of `subject` or `body` required
- Use `from_email` only for verified aliases in Gmail 'Send mail as' settings
1. `GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS` - Find the email/thread to reply to [Prerequisite]
- `thread_id` must be hex string; prefixes like 'msg-f:' are auto-stripped
2. `GMAIL_FETCH_MESSAGE_BY_MESSAGE_ID` - Get full message details for selected results [Optional]
- `query`: Gmail search syntax (from:, to:, subject:, is:unread, has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, b
- `include_payload`: Set `true` to get full message content
- Returns max ~500 per page; follow `nextPageToken` via `page_token` until absent
- `include_payload=true` on broad searches creates huge responses; default to metadata
1. `GMAIL_LIST_LABELS` - List all labels to find IDs and detect conflicts [Required]
- `label_name`: Max 225 chars, no commas, '/' for nesting (e.g., 'Work/Projects')
- `background_color`/`text_color`: Hex values from Gmail's predefined palette
1. `GMAIL_LIST_LABELS` - Get label IDs for custom labels [Prerequisite]
- `addLabelIds`: Array of label IDs to add
- `removeLabelIds`: Array of label IDs to remove
- `message_id`: 15-16 char hex string for single operations
- `message_id` must be 15-16 char hex, NOT UUIDs or web UI IDs
4. `GMAIL_SEND_DRAFT` - Send a draft (requires explicit user approval) [Optional]
- `subject`: Draft subject (omit for reply drafts to stay in thread)
- `thread_id`: For reply drafts (leave subject empty to stay in thread)
- Response includes `data.id` (draft_id) AND `data.message.id`; use `data.id` for draft operations
- Pass token as `page_token` in next request
- Continue until `nextPageToken` is absent or empty string
- `subject:invoice has:attachment after:2024/01/01` - Invoices with attachments this year
- `(from:alice OR from:bob) is:starred` - Starred emails from Alice or Bob
- Response data may be nested under `data_preview` or `data.messages`
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
| Create draft | GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT | recipient_email, subject, body, thread_id |

semantic_findings.title: High-Impact Gmail Actions Need Explicit Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill can send new emails, reply to threads, delete labels, bulk modify messages, and download attachments. Only draft sending mentions explicit approval, so agents may perform sensitive Gmail actions without a consistent confirmation gate.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflow lines directly describe outbound email, replies, deletion, bulk modification, and attachment access. Explicit approval is only stated for sending drafts, not for all high-impact actions.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Gmail OAuth Dependency
semantic_findings.description: Setup directs users to add the Rube MCP endpoint and complete Google OAuth through it. This grants a third-party service access to Gmail data and requires clear trust, scope, and revocation guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup section explicitly points users to the Rube MCP endpoint and a Gmail OAuth connection. This is legitimate functionality, but it is a real privacy and trust consideration.

content.user_title: Automate Gmail Workflows with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Gmail work often requires repeated searches, labels, drafts, and replies across many messages. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured Gmail workflows through Rube MCP.
actual_capabilities: Search Gmail messages with Gmail query syntax, pagination, labels, and payload options.
Resolve contacts, recipients, label IDs, message IDs, thread IDs, and draft IDs.
Create, update, send, and reply to emails through Gmail MCP tools.
Create, rename, delete, and color labels when Gmail permits those changes.
Apply or remove labels in bulk, including read, unread, archive, and category workflows.
Retrieve attachment references and use them in drafts or outbound email when supported.
limitations: Requires an active Rube MCP Gmail connection and Google OAuth authorization.
Does not provide Gmail credentials or bypass account permissions.
Gmail rate limits, size limits, and OAuth scopes still apply.
Broad searches with payloads can return large responses and may need pagination.

use_cases.title: Triage Customer Threads
use_cases.description: Find recent customer messages, summarize thread context, draft replies, and apply support labels after review.

use_cases.title: Organize Operations Mail
use_cases.description: Search for invoices, alerts, or project updates, then propose bulk label and archive actions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Executive Follow Ups
use_cases.description: Locate the right conversation, create a reviewed draft, and attach files from prior Gmail messages.

prompt_templates.title: Find Unread Emails
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gmail automation to find my unread messages from [sender] in the last [time period]. Show sender, subject, date, and message IDs before any other action.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Reply
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the latest thread about [topic], summarize the last message, and draft a reply for my review. Do not send the reply.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Project Mail
prompt_templates.prompt: List Gmail labels, find messages matching [query], propose label changes, and wait for my approval before applying bulk updates.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Mailbox Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Gmail for [query], fetch details only for selected results, identify attachments, prepare draft or label actions, and ask for confirmation before execution.

output_examples.input: Find unread invoices from last month.
output_examples.output: Found six unread invoice messages. The summary lists sender, subject, date, label status, and recommended next actions.

output_examples.input: Prepare a reply to the latest vendor renewal thread.
output_examples.output: Found the latest renewal thread, summarized the request, and prepared a concise reply draft for review. No email was sent.

output_examples.input: Clean up support notifications older than 30 days.
output_examples.output: Proposed a label and archive plan for matching notifications, including counts and sample subjects, and requested approval before changes.

best_practices: Confirm recipients, subject, body, and attachments before sending or replying.
Use narrow Gmail queries first, then fetch full payloads only for selected messages.
Resolve labels, message IDs, and thread IDs from Gmail responses before modifying data.
anti_patterns: Sending or replying before the user reviews final content and recipients.
Running broad payload searches across large mailboxes.
Using display names, web UI IDs, or guessed labels for destructive actions.

faq.question: Does this skill send email by itself?
faq.answer: It provides workflows for Gmail send and reply tools. Users should require confirmation before any outbound message.

faq.question: What connection is required?
faq.answer: Rube MCP must be connected, and Gmail OAuth must show an active account connection.

faq.question: Can it delete labels or change many messages?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes label deletion and bulk message modification, so use approvals and dry runs.

faq.question: Does it read attachments?
faq.answer: It can retrieve Gmail attachment references when the connected MCP tool supports that operation.

faq.question: Which assistants are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I verify before using it?
faq.answer: Verify OAuth scopes, Rube and Composio trust, recipient addresses, and all irreversible Gmail changes.
